title: Grounding and lightning
idea: Lightning takes the straightest path, so ground connections are short and direct with no sharp bends. Every ground rod is bonded together, and local electrical codes set the rules.

items: Short and direct. Avoid sharp bends
Bond them all together with heavy wire or conductive strap
Separate 8-foot ground rods for each leg, bonded to the tower and each other
On a grounded panel near where the feed lines enter the building
In series with the hot conductor only

cards.t: Keep ground connections short and direct
cards.why: That's good practice for lightning protection.

cards.t: Make every ground wire bend a right angle
cards.why: Sharp bends must be avoided, right angles included.

cards.t: Avoid sharp bends in grounding conductors
cards.why: Right. Sharp bends must be avoided.

cards.t: Bond all ground rods together with heavy wire or strap
cards.why: All external ground rods and earth connections get bonded together.

cards.t: Keep ground rods as far apart as possible, unbonded
cards.why: They should be bonded together, not kept separate.

cards.t: Separate 8-foot ground rods for each tower leg, bonded together
cards.why: That's the proper grounding method for a tower.

cards.t: Ground the tower to a cold-water pipe
cards.why: Use separate 8-foot ground rods for each leg, bonded to the tower and each other.

cards.t: Put the lightning arrester on a grounded panel where feed lines enter the building
Put the lightning arrester at the transceiver's output connector
cards.why: It goes on a grounded panel near where the feed lines enter the building.

cards.t: Bond at RF with flat copper strap
cards.why: Flat copper strap is the preferred conductor for RF bonding.

cards.t: Bond at RF with braid removed from coax
Fuse in series with the hot conductor only
cards.why: That's where a fuse or circuit breaker goes in a 120 V AC circuit.

cards.t: Fuse in the hot and the neutral conductors
cards.why: Only the hot conductor gets the fuse.

cards.t: Follow local electrical codes for tower grounding
cards.why: Local electrical codes set the grounding requirements, not FCC Part 97.

traps.wrong: At the output connector of a transceiver
traps.why: Not at the radio. On a grounded panel near where the feed lines come into the building.

traps.wrong: In series with the hot and neutral conductors
traps.why: Only the hot conductor gets the fuse, and it goes in series.

traps.wrong: Keep them as far apart as possible
traps.why: Ground rods get bonded together, not kept apart.

traps.wrong: Make sure all ground wire bends are right angles
traps.why: Right-angle bends are sharp bends. Keep connections short and direct.

traps.wrong: A connection between the tower base and a cold-water pipe
traps.why: A cold-water pipe isn't a tower ground. Use bonded 8-foot rods, one per leg.

traps.wrong: Wires must be carefully routed with precise right-angle bends
traps.why: Precise right-angle bends are exactly what to avoid.
FCC Part 97 doesn't set grounding rules. Local electrical codes do.

traps.wrong: Copper braid removed from coaxial cable
traps.why: Coax braid isn't the preferred RF bonding conductor. Flat copper strap is.
